profile.reading: QTS Richmond 2 (RIC2) is a data center campus in Sandston, Virginia, just east of Richmond and immediately adjacent to Richmond International Airport, developed by QTS Realty Trust (formerly Quality Technology Services, renamed following the company's 2013 IPO; this registry tracks both names as the same operator). Per QTS's own site, the campus spans approximately 85 acres and is planned to include five buildings once fully built out, with a total planned capacity of 180 megawatts of IT power upon completion; that figure describes the campus as a whole rather than any single building, and much of it was not yet in operation as of the source page, so it is not applied here as this building's own confirmed capacity. This building, DC3, sits at 6050 Technology Boulevard, one of five addressed buildings running along Technology Boulevard: 6030 (DC1), 6040 (DC2), 6050 (DC3), 6060 (DC5), and 6070 (DC6); the campus's own numbering skips DC4 entirely, a naming gap this registry notes rather than attempts to explain. RIC2 is QTS's second Richmond-area campus, distinct from the company's original Richmond 1 (RIC1) campus elsewhere in the metro, which this registry documents as a separate set of facilities. Henrico County, where Sandston sits, has become one of the mid-Atlantic's fastest-growing data center corridors in recent years, drawing hyperscale and colocation development on the strength of available land, Dominion Energy transmission capacity, and dense regional fiber routes running through the Richmond area. QTS's own campus page does not state which, if any, of the five RIC2 buildings are currently operating versus still under construction, and does not publish individual square footage, IT capacity, or year-opened figures for any single building on the campus; none of those figures is asserted here for DC3 specifically, consistent with this registry's practice of reporting only what the operator has actually confirmed at the building level.

reading.body:
RIC2 DC3 is one building on a planned 85-acre campus in Sandston, Virginia that QTS Realty Trust (formerly Quality Technology Services) intends to develop into 5 buildings with 180 MW of total capacity upon completion. The campus is not yet fully operating, so its contribution to published AI infrastructure capacity is currently zero. The planned 180 MW figure, if realized, would exceed the current total published capacity of Virginia by 13 percent and rank among the largest single campuses in the state.

The campus location places it in the Richmond metropolitan area, where QTS operates a separate, earlier Richmond 1 campus with 3 buildings. Virginia currently has 326 mapped data center facilities but only 23 with published power specifications, totaling 1,375 MW; RIC2 would add materially to a sparse published record in a state with substantial unmeasured capacity. The absence of published figures for current operating power means this facility cannot yet be assessed for its role in AI workload hosting.

Until RIC2 DC3 and its sister buildings reach operational status and their operators publish measured or committed power draws, the campus remains a planned resource. The 180 MW planned figure is the operator's own specification and reflects intent rather than current grid demand or AI-ready infrastructure. Readers tracking near-term AI scaling should monitor whether this campus moves from planned to operational status and what power density commitments QTS makes for AI-specific workloads.
